result.summary: The landlord approved this repair on two conditions: Harlow Heating only, and no more than £150. Neither option we have meets both. Harlow Heating is booked until 3 November, and Quick Fix Heating's quote is £230 from a different firm. So I have booked nobody. I emailed the landlord three options and asked them to choose (approval #35). I updated the tenant and put the case on hold with a follow-up in 2 days.
result.situation: The bedroom radiator at 27 Thistle Lane isn't heating, but the rest of the house is warm. The landlord approved the repair only with Harlow Heating and only up to £150 (event 003). Harlow Heating is fully booked until 3 November and offers an emergency visit at double rate, with no price given (event 004). Quick Fix Heating can come on Monday 6 October for £230 including parts (event 005).

escalation.recommendation: If the landlord hasn't replied by the follow-up date, chase them. If there's still no reply after that, or the tenant reports anyone vulnerable to the cold, escalate.

judgement.why_this_decision: The landlord said 'ONLY with Harlow Heating' and 'Max £150, nothing more without asking me first' (event 003). Quick Fix Heating breaks both conditions: it's a different firm and £80 over the limit. Harlow's emergency visit is at double rate with no price given, so it would probably go over £150. Waiting for Harlow is the only option within the approval, but it means a 4-week delay. That is the landlord's choice to make, so I asked them, in line with lessons #11 and #9.
